Strait of Hormuz Status: October 3, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  216 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
3 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Gulf News, WANA News Agency, NDTV Profit and Telegraph India report five Indian nationals were rescued after a projectile struck a Kuwait-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on October 1.

02 Al Jazeera reports UK maritime authorities say two oil tankers were hit by unknown projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz; WANA News Agency reports another tanker was struck in the same waterway.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; Brent stood at $102.25 as of 11:52 UTC, unchanged since the last session before the close.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with projectile strikes on merchant vessels continuing. Gulf News reports five Indian nationals were rescued with Oman's help after a Kuwait-flagged tanker was struck on October 1; NDTV Profit and Telegraph India carry the same rescue account. Al Jazeera reports UK maritime authorities say two oil tankers were hit by unknown projectiles near the strait; WANA News Agency reports another tanker was struck in the same waterway. The attacker has not been identified in any of these reports. These incidents follow the September 29 strikes on three vessels, including a crude oil tanker and an LNG tanker, and the separate hit on a Kuwait Oil Tanker Company supertanker on October 1, both covered in earlier reporting. WANA News Agency reports seven tankers were targeted in five days in the strait, a figure no major wire in this feed has separately addressed. Forty-four events have been indexed in the last 24 hours. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.25 as of 11:52 UTC; futures are closed and the -0.11% figure is the change in the last session before the close, not a move in the last session before the close. WTI was last quoted at $91.11. As of 11:50 UTC, 91 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
